units.title: Functions and Graphs
topics: Eight ways functions are used in computing

sections.title: Eight ways functions are used in computing

summary: A function pairs each input with exactly one output; domain and range come from restrictions of the formula.
Even and odd symmetry, composition and inverses are the algebra of functions.
Transformations shift, stretch and reflect graphs; knowing them saves plotting.
Exponent, logarithm and trigonometric rules are the toolkit used in every later unit.

units.title: Limits and Continuity
topics: Limits at infinity and infinite limits
Eight uses of limits in computing and daily life

sections.title: Limits at infinity and infinite limits
Eight uses of limits in computing and daily life

summary: A limit describes the approached value and ignores the value at the point; both one-sided limits must agree.
For (0)/(0), factor, rationalise or use a standard limit; for x → ∞ divide by the highest power.
Continuity means the graph can be drawn without lifting the pen; the three kinds of break are removable, jump and infinite.
The IVT guarantees roots of continuous functions between sign changes.

units.title: Differentiation
summary: The derivative is the limit of difference quotients, equal to the slope of the tangent.
A small table plus four rules (sum, product, quotient, chain) handles nearly every function.
Implicit, logarithmic and parametric methods cover curves not written as y = f (x).
Higher derivatives and nth-derivative formulas appear in series and in applications.

units.title: Applications of Derivatives
topics: Rates of change and related rates
Eight uses of the applications of derivatives

sections.title: Rates of change and related rates
Eight uses of the applications of derivatives

summary: The derivative gives tangents, rates, and the shape of a graph (increasing, decreasing, concave).
Optimisation reduces a real problem to one variable and tests critical points and endpoints.
Rolle and the MVT link the average slope to an instantaneous slope; L'Hôpital turns indeterminate limits into derivative quotients.
Taylor series replace a function by polynomials and enable numerical approximation.

units.title: Integration
topics: The definite integral and the Fundamental Theorem

sections.title: The definite integral and the Fundamental Theorem

summary: Integration is reverse differentiation; always add C for indefinite integrals and verify by differentiating.
Substitution undoes the chain rule, parts undoes the product rule, partial fractions handle rational functions.
The Fundamental Theorem lets us compute definite integrals from antiderivatives.
Areas, volumes, averages and total change are all definite integrals; improper integrals are limits.

units.title: Differential Equations
topics: Second-order linear equations with constant coefficients

sections.title: Second-order linear equations with constant coefficients

summary: The order sets the number of constants; initial conditions pick a particular solution.
Separable, homogeneous, linear and exact first-order equations each have a systematic method.
Constant-coefficient second-order equations reduce to an auxiliary quadratic whose roots give exponentials, polynomial-times-exponential, or oscillations.
Growth, decay and cooling are first-order linear models with exponential solutions.
